<reason>A won by distinguishing an open default from unconditional release and defending advance exceptions covering genuine investment needs, including integrated projects. B identified a credible risk to commercialization, but repeatedly asserted that partners would withdraw without explaining why A’s pre-funding assessment would uniquely cause that result. Its later objections to delayed waivers and file-by-file petitions did not address A’s actual proposal. A consequently preserved the decisive comparative benefit: guaranteed reuse for publicly funded outputs where no sufficient reason for restriction exists.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s closing turned B’s demand that justification belong in the project bargain against it: A already allowed that assessment before funding. Coupled with B’s concession that exclusivity needs must be real, this substantially weakened B’s claim that the open default necessarily destroys collaborations.</best_rebuttal>
